text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the recent ant bite, I need to check if you have experienced any recent gastrointestinal symptoms like diarrhea or abdominal pain. Are you currently taking any immunosuppressive medications for your Crohn's or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pitting edema and dilated tortuous veins strongly suggests underlying venous insufficiency complicating the healing of this lesion. To rule out an infectious cause like ecthyma gangrenosum or atypical mycobacteria, I will order a tissue culture and pathology. REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture_and_Pathology_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing neutrophilic infiltration without infection are classic for pyoderma gangrenosum, especially given your history of Crohn's disease.
